shipped_video_records.what_happens: What is a seed?: A seed is a tiny plant waiting to wake up. Inside every seed is a baby plant and a snack of food to help it start growing. Seeds come in all shapes and sizes — some tiny like a dot, some big like a bean. When a seed gets soil, water, and warmth, it wakes up and starts to grow!

other_factors.bibliography_youtube_alternate: SciShow Kids — How Does A Seed Become A Plant?

shipped_video_records.source_title: Ken-Burns pan of in-game portrait/tile art
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Soil and garden beds: Soil is like a cozy bed and a kitchen for plants, all in one. It holds water and food that roots drink up. Good garden soil is soft and crumbly, so roots can stretch out. Gardeners rake their beds nice and smooth before planting, so every seed has a comfy home.

other_factors.bibliography_youtube_alternate: SciShow Kids — Let's Plant a Garden!

shipped_video_records.place_in_game: Knowledge star `03_planting` — "How to plant a seed" (zone=beds)
shipped_video_records.what_happens: How to plant a seed: Planting a seed is easy and fun! First, poke a little hole in the soil with your finger. Drop the seed in, and tuck it in with a blanket of soil. Give it a gentle drink of water, and say good night, little seed — see you when you sprout!

other_factors.bibliography_youtube_alternate: Ivan Inspects — Planting Seeds For Kids

shipped_video_records.source_title: Ken-Burns pan of in-game portrait/tile art
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Watering plants: Plants get thirsty, just like you! Their roots drink water from the soil and send it all the way up to the leaves. A gentle sprinkle is best — too much water can make roots soggy. The best time to water the garden is in the cool morning, before the sun gets hot.

other_factors.bibliography_youtube_alternate: Goally — How to Water the Plants for Kids

shipped_video_records.what_happens: Seeds sprouting: When a seed wakes up, we say it sprouts! First a little root grows down, down, down into the soil. Then a green shoot pushes up, up, up toward the light. The first tiny leaves unfold like little hands saying hello to the sun!

other_factors.bibliography_youtube_alternate: SciShow Kids — Watch a Seed Sprout!

shipped_video_records.what_happens: Sunlight and growing: Sunlight is plant food power! Leaves catch sunshine and use it to make sugar — that is how plants make their own lunch. This special trick is called photosynthesis. That is why plants lean toward the light, and why gardens love sunny days!

Watching plants grow: Plants grow a little bit every single day. First comes the sprout, then more leaves, then the plant grows tall and strong. Some plants grow flowers, and the flowers turn into fruits and vegetables. Be patient, water often, and watch the magic happen!

shipped_video_records.source_title: Ken-Burns pan of in-game portrait/tile art
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Uprooting and clearing space: Sometimes a garden gets crowded, and plants have to share too much. Weeds sneak in and gobble up the water and sunlight our vegetables need. Gardeners gently pull them out, roots and all. With more room, our garden plants grow bigger and happier!

Harvesting the garden: Harvest time is the best part of gardening! It is when the fruits and vegetables are ripe and ready to pick. We pull carrots, snap beans, and twist tomatoes gently off the vine. Then we get to eat the yummy food we grew ourselves!

shipped_video_records.source_title: One Year. One Tree. One Drone.webm
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Seasons in the garden: The garden changes with the seasons. In spring we plant seeds, and in summer everything grows tall in the sunshine. In fall we harvest, and leaves turn orange and red. In winter the garden rests under the frost, dreaming of spring!

shipped_video_records.source_title: Ken-Burns pan of in-game portrait/tile art
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Garden animals: A farm garden is full of animal friends. Chickens give us eggs, and cows give us milk. Dogs keep watch, and rabbits hop around looking for greens to nibble. Taking care of animals every day is a big part of life on a farm!

shipped_video_records.source_title: Ken-Burns pan of in-game portrait/tile art
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Storing the harvest: After the harvest, we save food to enjoy later. Pumpkins and potatoes keep for months in a cool, dark place. Some fruits become jam, and some vegetables become pickles! Storing food means we can taste our summer garden even in winter.

other_factors.bibliography_youtube_alternate: How we store ONE year's worth of Homegrown Food

shipped_video_records.what_happens: Chickens are curious birds that live together in a flock. They scratch the dirt with their feet to find seeds and tasty bugs. A mother hen lays about one egg every day, and she loves a cozy nest. Chickens even take baths in dust to keep their feathers clean!

shipped_video_records.place_in_game: Pen animal reveal (Buddy video skipped in gameplay)
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Rabbits have long ears that can turn almost all the way around to listen. Their big front teeth never stop growing, so they nibble all day long. Rabbits hop fast and dig cozy burrows underground. On a farm, rabbits munch on grass, carrots, and leafy greens.

shipped_video_records.place_in_game: Pen animal reveal (Buddy video skipped in gameplay)
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Pigs are some of the smartest animals on a farm. They use their strong snouts to sniff and dig for food. Pigs roll in the mud to stay cool — it works like nature's sunscreen. A happy pig wags its curly tail, just like a puppy!

shipped_video_records.place_in_game: Pen animal reveal (Buddy video skipped in gameplay)
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Cows are gentle giants that spend the whole day munching grass. A cow has a special tummy with four parts to help digest her food. Cows give us milk, which becomes cheese, butter, and ice cream. Every cow has her own pattern of spots — no two are the same!

shipped_video_records.place_in_game: Pen animal reveal (Buddy video skipped in gameplay)
shipped_video_records.source_title: Ken-Burns pan of in-game portrait/tile art
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Farm dogs are hard workers and best friends. They help round up the animals and keep everyone safe. A dog can smell about ten thousand times better than you can! At the end of the day, a farm dog loves a good belly rub.

This is the chicken coop, where the hens sleep and lay their eggs. Every morning, farmers gently lift the eggs out of the nesting boxes. The hens keep their eggs warm and cozy in the soft straw. Fresh eggs get washed and kept cool — ready for breakfast!

shipped_video_records.source_title: 2022-06-02 LJUBLJANA Karlovško predmestje COCCINELLIDAE Cucujoidea PIKAPOLONICA.webm
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Ladybugs are a gardener's best helpers. One ladybug can munch fifty aphids in a single day, and that protects our plants. Their bright red shells warn birds to stay away. When ladybugs fly, their spotted shells lift up like tiny doors!

Rolly pollies curl into a tiny ball when they feel shy. They are not insects at all — they are cousins of crabs! They eat old leaves and turn them into fresh soil for the garden. Rolly pollies love damp, cozy places under rocks and logs.

Earthworms are underground gardeners. As they wiggle, they dig little tunnels so plant roots get air and water. Worms eat old leaves and leave behind rich food for the soil. A worm has no eyes, but it can still feel light and shadows!

Honeybees visit hundreds of flowers every single day. They carry yellow pollen from flower to flower, which helps plants make seeds and fruit. Bees do a waggle dance to tell their friends where the best flowers are! Without bees, we would have far fewer strawberries and pumpkins.

A butterfly starts life as a very hungry caterpillar. Inside its chrysalis it changes completely — that big change is called metamorphosis. Butterflies taste with their feet when they land on flowers! They sip sweet nectar and help flowers make seeds.

Ants are tiny but mighty — an ant can carry things fifty times heavier than itself! They live in big families and talk by touching antennas. Their tunnels help air and water reach plant roots. Watch an ant line closely — they follow smell trails their friends left behind.

shipped_video_records.source_title: Ken-Burns pan of in-game portrait/tile art
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Aphids are tiny green bugs that sip juice from plant stems. Too many aphids can make a plant droopy and sad. That is why gardeners love ladybugs — they gobble aphids up! Ants sometimes look after aphids like little cows, for their sweet honeydew.

shipped_video_records.source_title: Time-lapse of a caterpillar eating a basil.ogv
shipped_video_records.what_happens: A caterpillar's job is to eat, eat, eat! It sheds its skin as it grows bigger and bigger. One day it will build a chrysalis and become a butterfly or a moth. Some caterpillars nibble garden leaves, so gardeners keep a friendly eye on them.

Garden spiders are quiet helpers. They spin sticky silk webs to catch flies and moths that bother our plants. Spider silk is stronger than steel of the same size! Most garden spiders are gentle and shy — they would rather hide than say hello.

Grasshoppers have big back legs that work like springs. They can jump twenty times their own body length! Grasshoppers sing by rubbing their legs against their wings. You can hear them chirping in the warm summer grass.

shipped_video_records.source_title: Snail crawling on a leaf in Asuka Village, Nara, Japan (May 2025).webm
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Snails carry their homes on their backs. They glide along on one big foot, leaving a shiny, silvery trail. A snail's shell grows bigger as the snail grows. On rainy days, snails come out to explore the garden!

The praying mantis folds its front legs like it is saying please. It can turn its head almost all the way around — no other insect can do that! A mantis stays still as a statue, then catches garden pests quick as a flash. Gardeners love the mantis because it protects their plants.

Lettuce grows in leafy green bundles. Farmers cut the whole head close to the soil with a small knife. Lettuce is mostly water, so it is extra crunchy and fresh. It is the start of almost every salad!

shipped_video_records.source_title: Black-eyed pea pods on plant in Hong Kong.jpg
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Peas grow in little green pods that hang from climbing vines. Farmers pick the pods when they feel plump and full. Pop one open — the peas sit in a row like beads! Peas give you energy to run and play.
shipped_video_records.why_used: First-harvest ceremony for Pea — POOR FIT: Black-eyed pea photo

shipped_video_records.what_happens: Radishes are one of the fastest vegetables to grow — about one month! Farmers pull them up by their leaves, just like carrots. They are crunchy with a tiny spicy zing. Radishes come in red, pink, purple, and even white!

Crunchy carrots grow under the ground. Farmers hold the green leafy tops and pull gently until the carrot pops out. Carrots are full of vitamin A, which helps your eyes see well. Rabbits agree — carrots are delicious!

Spinach has soft dark-green leaves packed with iron. Farmers cut the outer leaves so the plant keeps growing in the middle. Spinach helps your muscles stay strong. Popeye was right — spinach is a power food!

Onions grow underground in layers, like a tiny ball. Farmers wait until the green tops flop over, then dig them up carefully. Onions make soups and sauces taste amazing. They can also make your eyes water!

A cabbage is a big round ball of tightly packed leaves. Farmers cut the thick stem at the bottom and lift the whole head. Cabbage stays fresh a long time. We eat it in salads, soups, and even sauerkraut!

Strawberries are ready when they turn ruby red all over. Farmers pinch the stem so the soft berry does not get squished. Strawberries have more vitamin C than oranges! They are the only fruit with seeds on the outside.

shipped_video_records.source_title: A farmer explaining a good tomato harvest.webm
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Tomatoes turn from green to bright red as they ripen in the sun. Farmers twist them gently off the vine so the plant keeps growing more. Tomatoes are full of vitamins that keep your heart strong. We eat them in salads, sauces, and soups!

shipped_video_records.source_title: Aerial view of corn harvesting in Northern Illinois USA.webm
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Corn grows taller than a grown-up! Each ear is wrapped in a leafy husk with silky threads on top. Farmers snap the ear down and twist to pick it. Every silk thread is connected to one kernel of corn!

shipped_video_records.source_title: A unique combine to harvest cucumbers was displayed for the press (FL45798464).jpg
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Cucumbers hang from vines like little green boats. Farmers snip them off while they are still firm and crunchy. Cucumbers are cool and refreshing — almost all water. They are perfect for a summer snack!
shipped_video_records.why_used: First-harvest ceremony for Cucumber — POOR FIT: Machinery press photo

shipped_video_records.source_title: Black-eyed pea pods on plant in Hong Kong.jpg
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Beans grow in long pods on climbing vines or bushy plants. Farmers pick the pods when they are bright green and snap easily. Inside are soft beans that help you grow strong. Some beans we dry and keep for winter!
shipped_video_records.why_used: First-harvest ceremony for Bean — POOR FIT: Reused black-eyed pea photo

shipped_video_records.source_title: Starr-200618-7750-Capsicum annuum-red bell pepper harvest from veggie garden-Hawea Pl Olinda-Maui (50336358332).jpg
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Bell peppers start green and can turn yellow, orange, or red in the sun. Farmers clip the stem so the plant keeps making more. Peppers are crunchy and sweet, and full of vitamin C. They look like little colorful bells!

Zucchini is a summer squash that grows fast on a bushy plant. Farmers pick them when they are still small and tender. Leave one too long and it becomes a giant! Zucchini is delicious grilled, baked, or in bread.

shipped_video_records.source_title: Drukte bij de fruitoogst in het Westland Weeknummer 42-33 - Open Beelden - 14138.ogv
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Melons grow on vines that sprawl across the warm soil. Farmers know a melon is ready when it smells sweet and the stem slips off easily. Inside is juicy fruit that cools you down on a hot day. Melons are mostly water — and kids love them!

Eggplants are shiny purple fruits that hang from a sturdy plant. Farmers cut them with a little stem still attached. Inside the purple skin is soft pale flesh. Eggplant soaks up flavors in stews and sauces!
shipped_video_records.why_used: First-harvest ceremony for Eggplant — POOR FIT: Food demo not harvest

shipped_video_records.source_title: Pie Pumpkin Harvest near Princeville, Illinois USA.jpg
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Pumpkins grow on long vines that crawl across the ground. Farmers cut the thick stem and leave a little handle on top. Pumpkins can grow bigger than you! We eat them in pies and soups, and carve them for fun.

Potatoes grow underground on the roots of the plant. Farmers dig carefully so they do not poke the tubers. One plant can hide a whole handful of potatoes! They become mashed potatoes, fries, and baked potatoes.

Broccoli is a tight cluster of tiny green flower buds. Farmers cut the thick stem before the buds open into yellow flowers. Broccoli is packed with vitamins. Those little green trees on your plate are flower buds!
shipped_video_records.why_used: First-harvest ceremony for Broccoli — POOR FIT: Holiday still-life

shipped_video_records.what_happens: Cauliflower grows a big white head protected by green leaves. Farmers fold the leaves over the head to keep it pale, then cut it when it is firm. Cauliflower can be mashed, roasted, or eaten raw with dip!

shipped_video_records.source_title: Grape harvest in Chateaux Luna vineyard 2.jpg
shipped_video_records.what_happens: Grapes grow in bunches on woody vines. Farmers snip whole clusters when the berries are sweet and plump. Some grapes become juice, and some become raisins. Grapes come in green, red, and purple!

Raspberries grow on canes with soft thorns. Farmers pick the berries when they slip off the core easily and leave a little hollow. Raspberries are fragile and sweet. They stain your fingers bright pink!
shipped_video_records.why_used: First-harvest ceremony for Raspberry — POOR FIT: Static plant photo

shipped_video_records.what_happens: Turnips are round roots that grow under leafy green tops. Farmers pull them up by the greens when the roots feel firm. Both the root and the leaves can be eaten! Turnips have a mild, earthy taste.
Celery grows tall crisp stalks from a bunch in the soil. Farmers cut the whole plant at the base. The crunchy stalks are mostly water and make a great snack. Celery leaves are tasty in soups too!

Garlic grows as a bulb of little cloves under the ground. Farmers dig the bulbs when the tops turn brown and dry them in the sun. One clove planted in fall becomes a whole new bulb! Garlic makes almost every savory dish better.
Leeks look like giant green onions with long white stems. Farmers mound soil around them so the stems stay white and sweet, then dig them carefully. Leeks are mild and delicious in soups and pies!
shipped_video_records.why_used: First-harvest ceremony for Leek — POOR FIT: Ornamental allium

shipped_video_records.what_happens: Kale has curly or flat dark-green leaves full of vitamins. Farmers pick the outer leaves so the plant keeps growing. Kale is tough when raw but soft when cooked. It is one of the strongest greens in the garden!
An artichoke is a big flower bud that never opens. Farmers cut the bud with a short stem before it blooms into a purple thistle. We eat the soft base of each leaf and the heart in the middle!

Wheat grows in golden fields that wave in the wind. Farmers harvest the tall stalks with a big machine called a combine. The tiny grains inside become flour for bread. Almost every loaf starts as a wheat plant!

Chili peppers grow upright on bushy plants and can be mild or fiery hot. Farmers pick them when they turn bright red, orange, or yellow. Capsaicin is the chemical that makes chilies spicy. Handle them carefully — and wash your hands!

Blueberries grow on woody bushes in clusters of little blue orbs. Farmers roll them gently into their hands when they are deep blue and sweet. Blueberries are packed with antioxidants. They are perfect in muffins, pancakes, and by the handful!

Oats grow in soft grassy fields with dangling grain heads. Farmers cut and dry the stalks, then separate the oat grains. Those grains become oatmeal for breakfast! Oats give you long-lasting energy to play.
